examples.ko: 새 한 쌍이 처마 밑에 깃들였어요.
examples.en: A pair of birds nested under the eaves.

examples.ko: 이 노래에는 어머니의 사랑이 깃들여 있어요.
examples.en: A mother's love dwells in this song.
I observed the animals that make their home in the old forest.

examples.ko: 선물에 정성이 깃들인 것 같아서 고마웠어요.
examples.en: I was thankful because the gift seemed full of sincere care.

examples.ko: 작은 집에 가족의 추억이 깃들이기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Family memories began to settle into the small house.

examples.ko: 이 그림에는 작가의 슬픔이 깃들이어 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: The artist's sorrow seems to dwell in this painting.

explain: 새가 둥지를 틀고 사는 것에서, 정성, 추억, 역사, 감정이 어떤 곳에 스며 있다는 뜻으로도 써요. 주로 글이나 설명에서 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '담겨 있다'를 더 많이 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '깃들다'도 있어요.
explain_en: Starting from birds nesting somewhere, it is also used when care, memories, history or feelings are present in a place or thing. It is mostly used in writing and explanations; in everyday talk people more often say '담겨 있다'. A similar word is '깃들다'.

examples.en: The eastern sky slowly grew bright.
The sun is rising in the east.

examples.ko: 우리는 동녘이 트기 전에 산에 올랐어요.
examples.en: We climbed the mountain before the eastern sky began to lighten.
At dawn I opened the window facing east.
I made a wish while looking toward the east.

examples.ko: 동녘의 첫 햇살이 바다를 붉게 물들였어요.
examples.en: The first sunlight in the east dyed the sea red.

explain: '동쪽'과 같은 방향이지만 시나 글에서 많이 쓰고, 해가 뜨는 새벽 하늘 느낌이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '동쪽'이 자연스럽고, 반대는 '서녘'이에요.
explain_en: It points to the same direction as '동쪽', but is common in poems and writing and carries the feel of the dawn sky where the sun rises. In daily conversation '동쪽' is more natural, and the opposite is '서녘'.

examples.en: If you shout in the mountains, it echoes.
In an empty gym even small sounds echo.
His words are still echoing in my ears.
The sound of the bell echoed long through the valley.
The singing echoed loudly inside the tunnel.

examples.ko: 친구 이름을 부르자 목소리가 메아리쳐 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: When I called my friend's name, my voice came back as an echo.

explain: 소리가 부딪혀서 되돌아와 울리는 것을 말해요. 산에서 '야호!' 하고 외치면 돌아오는 소리가 '메아리'예요. 잊히지 않고 마음에 계속 남는 말을 '귓가에 메아리치다'처럼 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It means a sound bounces back and rings out again. The sound that returns when you shout '야호!' in the mountains is a '메아리'. It is also used figuratively, as in '귓가에 메아리치다', for words that stay with you.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 우유 위에 거품이 몽글몽글 올라왔어요.
examples.en: Soft, small bubbles puffed up on top of the warm milk.
Soft, round clouds are floating in the sky.
The soft tofu is bubbling away in soft curds.
A soft excitement is blooming in my heart.

examples.ko: 비누 거품이 몽글몽글 생겨서 아이가 좋아해요.
examples.en: Soft soap bubbles are forming, and the child loves it.
I watched the puffs of smoke rising for a long time.

explain: 작고 부드러운 덩어리가 동글동글 모이거나 피어오르는 모습에 써요. 거품, 구름, 연기처럼 눈에 보이는 것뿐 아니라 '마음이 몽글몽글하다'처럼 따뜻하고 간질간질한 감정에도 써요.
explain_en: It describes small, soft clumps gathering or rising in a round shape, such as bubbles, clouds and smoke. It is also used for warm, fluttery feelings, as in '마음이 몽글몽글하다'.

examples.en: The fallen leaves rustle in the wind.
The plastic bag keeps rustling and it bothers me.

examples.ko: 밤새 쥐가 바스락거리는 소리에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep because of a mouse rustling all night.

examples.ko: 마른 풀을 밟으면 바스락거리는 소리가 나요.
examples.en: When you step on dry grass, it makes a rustling sound.
The child played rustling around under the blanket.

examples.ko: 종이가 바스락거리지 않게 조심히 넘겨 주세요.
examples.en: Please turn the pages carefully so the paper doesn't rustle.

explain: '바스락' 소리가 계속 나거나 반복될 때 써요. '바스락'이 한 번 나는 소리라면 '바스락거리다'는 이어지는 소리예요. 밤에 방해되는 소리나 조용한 곳에서 들리는 작은 소리에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when the '바스락' sound continues or repeats. '바스락' is a single sound, while '바스락거리다' is an ongoing one. It often appears for small noises heard in a quiet place or at night.

en: in small beads; beading (of sweat, dew)

examples.ko: 달리기를 했더니 이마에 땀이 송알송알 맺혔어요.
examples.en: After running, beads of sweat formed on my forehead.

examples.ko: 아침에 풀잎마다 이슬이 송알송알 맺혀 있어요.
examples.en: In the morning, dew has formed in tiny drops on every blade of grass.

examples.ko: 차가운 컵 겉에 물방울이 송알송알 생겼어요.
examples.en: Little water droplets formed on the outside of the cold cup.

examples.ko: 아이 코끝에 땀방울이 송알송알 맺힌 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw tiny beads of sweat on the child's nose tip.

examples.ko: 창문에 송알송알 맺힌 빗방울이 참 예뻐요.
examples.en: The raindrops dotting the window are so pretty.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 국을 먹었더니 코에 땀이 송알송알 나요.
examples.en: After eating the hot soup, sweat is beading on my nose.

explain: 땀, 이슬, 물방울 같은 작은 방울이 여기저기 맺힌 모습에 써요. 거의 '맺히다'와 같이 나오니 '땀이 송알송알 맺히다'를 한 덩어리로 외우세요. 땀에는 '송골송골'도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It describes small drops such as sweat, dew or water beads forming in many places. It almost always appears with '맺히다', so learn '땀이 송알송알 맺히다' as one chunk. For sweat, '송골송골' is also commonly used.

examples.en: My mother's face keeps flickering before my eyes.
A shadow flickered outside the window and it startled me.
The moonlight is shimmering on the water.
I was sleepy and the letters in the book swam before my eyes.

examples.ko: 커튼 뒤에서 누가 어른거리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It looks like someone is moving faintly behind the curtain.

examples.ko: 밤새 아이 모습이 눈에 어른거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The child's image kept haunting me all night, so I couldn't sleep.

explain: 희미하게 보였다 안 보였다 하거나, 보고 싶은 사람의 모습이 자꾸 떠오를 때 써요. '아른거리다'와 비슷한 말이고, '눈앞에', '눈에'와 같이 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is used when something appears and disappears faintly, or when the image of someone you miss keeps coming to mind. '아른거리다' is a similar word, and it is often used with '눈앞에' or '눈에'.

examples.ko: 물살이 빠른 여울에서 아이들이 물놀이를 했어요.
examples.en: The children played in the water at the fast-flowing shallows.

examples.ko: 이 여울은 물이 얕아서 걸어서 건널 수 있어요.
examples.en: The water in this shallow stretch of rapids is low, so you can cross it on foot.

examples.ko: 여울 소리가 시원해서 한참 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: The sound of the rapids was so refreshing that I sat there for a while.

examples.ko: 낚시꾼들이 여울을 따라 천천히 걸어 올라갔어요.
examples.en: The anglers slowly walked upstream along the rapids.

examples.ko: 강이 좁아지는 곳에 작은 여울이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A small stretch of rapids formed where the river narrows.
The fish are gathered below the rapids.

explain: 강바닥이 얕거나 좁아서 물살이 빠르고 소리가 나는 곳이에요. 글이나 노래에서 풍경을 그릴 때 어울리는 말이에요. 좁아져서 물이 세게 흐르는 곳은 '여울목'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a place in a river where the bed is shallow or narrow, so the current runs fast and makes noise. It suits writing and songs that paint a landscape. A narrowed spot where water rushes is also called '여울목'.

examples.en: I can hear a katydid in the grass.
The child caught a katydid and put it in a container.
Katydids hop around the meadow.

examples.ko: 여름밤에 여치가 울면 시골 생각이 나요.
examples.en: When katydids sing on a summer night, I think of the countryside.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 풀로 여치 집을 만들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandfather made me a katydid house out of grass.
Katydids and bush crickets look alike.

explain: 메뚜기, 베짱이처럼 풀밭에 사는 곤충이에요. 우는 소리는 입이 아니라 날개를 비벼서 내는 소리인데, 한국어로는 그냥 '울다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is an insect of the grass, like the grasshopper and the bush cricket. Its song comes from rubbing its wings, but Korean simply says it '울다' (cries).

examples.en: The road is bumpy, so it's hard to walk.
I could see bulging muscles on his arm.
My facial skin has become bumpy, and I'm worried.
After the rain stopped, the dirt road is lumpy.
The trunk of an old tree looks knobby.
I fixed the bumpy wall so it's smooth.

explain: 표면이 평평하지 않고 군데군데 불거져 나온 모습이에요. 길, 근육, 피부, 나무껍질처럼 겉이 고르지 않은 것에 써요. 반대로 표면이 고를 때는 '매끈하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It describes a surface that is not flat and has bumps sticking out here and there. It is used for roads, muscles, skin and tree bark whose surface is uneven. The opposite, for an even surface, is '매끈하다'.

examples.ko: 방 안에 향초 냄새가 은은히 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: The scent of the candle spread softly through the room.
A bell can be heard faintly in the distance.
The moonlight shines gently on the lake.

examples.ko: 그 꽃은 은은히 좋은 향이 나요.
examples.en: That flower has a soft, pleasant fragrance.
Her softly smiling face was really pretty.

examples.ko: 은은히 켜 둔 조명 덕분에 분위기가 좋아요.
examples.en: Thanks to the softly lit lights, the mood is nice.

explain: 소리, 빛, 향기가 뚜렷하지 않고 부드럽게 느껴질 때 써요. 형용사 '은은하다'는 '은은한 향기'처럼 꾸며 주는 말로 쓰고, 좋은 느낌으로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when a sound, light or scent isn't strong but is felt softly. The adjective '은은하다' is used as in '은은한 향기' (a subtle fragrance), and it usually has a positive feel.

examples.en: When the wind blew, the ripples on the lake swayed.
I read a book in a room with a flickering candle.
Longing stirs inside my heart.
The sea, with the water shimmering in the sunlight, was beautiful.
The flame flickered and then soon went out.
The shadows of leaves outside the window sway on the wall.

explain: '흔들리다'는 한 번 크게 움직여도 쓰지만, '일렁이다'는 물결이나 불꽃이 작게 반복해서 출렁이는 모습이에요. '그리움이 일렁이다'처럼 마음이 잔잔히 흔들릴 때도 써요. 활용은 '일렁여요', '일렁였어요'예요.
explain_en: '흔들리다' can describe a single big movement, but '일렁이다' describes ripples or flames moving in small, repeated swells. It is also used for a heart gently stirring, as in '그리움이 일렁이다'. It conjugates as '일렁여요' and '일렁였어요'.

examples.en: The ripples moved in gentle waves and sparkled.
The candle flame is flickering and swaying.
Moonlight spreads shimmering over the sea.
I stared for a long time at the flames dancing and flickering.
The shadows wavered on the wall.
Sunlight shines in the water in wavering patterns.

explain: '일렁일렁 흔들리다', '일렁일렁 움직이다'처럼 동사 앞에서 흔들리는 모습을 꾸며요. 물결이나 불빛이 부드럽게 반복해서 움직이는 장면에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It goes before a verb to describe how something moves, as in '일렁일렁 흔들리다' or '일렁일렁 움직이다'. It suits scenes where ripples or light keep moving softly and repeatedly.

examples.en: The cherry blossoms are in full bloom in the park.
I took photos while walking along the path of blossoms in full bloom.
The roses are blooming profusely in the yard, so it is full of fragrance.
Butterflies flit among the flowers in full bloom.
The azaleas are in splendid full bloom this year.
At the feast, people had a wild, lively time.

explain: 꽃이 탐스럽게 활짝 핀 모습에 가장 많이 쓰고, 보통 '흐드러지게 피다'로 말해요. 잔치나 놀이가 한창 무르익은 분위기를 말할 때도 '흐드러지게 놀다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is used most often for flowers blooming lushly and fully, usually as '흐드러지게 피다'. It can also describe a party or play at its liveliest, as in '흐드러지게 놀다'.
